results.reason: The response identifies the Varga acquisition as a Change of Control that requires Crestline's prior written consent under DA §15.4. It says Part 3.5 wrongly describes the agreement as 'notice only; no consent required.' It explains the exposure: a termination right, a termination fee, and an inaccurate consents representation.

The response explains that §14.2, read with the §1.1 'Qualified Transferee' definition, lets Crestline assign without Halvorsen's consent to any lab or diagnostic distributor in the Territory. It notes this could include a competitor or a competitor's affiliate because the definition has no competitor exclusion.

The response states that First Amendment §3.1 restates §12.3 so that only §9 confidentiality breaches are carved out, dropping the §10 IP and §11 indemnity carve-outs. It says the amendment controls under §17.5 order of precedence, so those claims are now capped.
The response states that the original §12.3 excluded breaches of §9, breaches of §10, and indemnification obligations under §11.
The response states that the §12.2 cap is the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The response is a memo with separate issues. Each issue has headings for Document/Section, Why it matters for Halvorsen, and Recommended fix.
The negative criterion is met (pass): the response expressly concludes that consent is required and that the notice-only description is wrong.
The response expressly states that the original carve-outs no longer apply unless a further amendment is signed.
